meta.title: Owler — your scheduled jobs, watched from the editor
meta.description: A Mac app that lists the jobs you run on launchd and keeps the result of every run. Open any run in Claude Code inside Cursor or VS Code.

hero.tagline: Your scheduled jobs, watched from the editor.

product.title: Open last night's run in the morning.
product.statement: A claude -p every morning, an import every evening. Every run is kept.
product.statementMuted: Dig into any of them with Claude Code, right in your editor.
product.label: What it does

items.title: A record of every run
items.body: Start, end, exit code and output, every time.

items.title: claude -p's report
items.body: When a job runs claude -p, its last message shows on the run's page.

items.title: Cursor and VS Code
items.body: Brings the job's folder to the front and opens a Claude Code conversation there.

items.title: Set jobs up with Claude
items.body: Decide what to run and when, and Claude registers it.

items.title: Menu bar
items.body: The last result of each job, with a count of failures.

install.title: Install, talk it through, let it run.

steps.title: Install
steps.body: Download the DMG and drag Owler into Applications. Homebrew works too.

steps.title: Let it open
steps.body: The author is not a registered Apple developer, so the first launch is blocked. Click Open Anyway in System Settings → Privacy & Security.

steps.title: Add a job
steps.body: Click New Job at the bottom left of the window and talk it through with Claude Code.

install.accessibility: Allow Accessibility access when asked. Owler uses it to bring the editor window to the front.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Owler runs the jobs you register on launchd and shows their records. That is all it does. There is no server, no analytics and no account.

sections.title: What it reads and writes
sections.body: Job definitions, and the record and output of each run, live in ~/Library/Application Support/Owler. The launchd agents live in ~/Library/LaunchAgents. When a job runs claude -p, Owler looks for that folder's Claude Code transcript and reads the last message. To find the editor window, it reads the titles of Cursor and VS Code windows.

sections.title: Nothing leaves your Mac
sections.body: Every record stays on this Mac. Nothing is collected and nothing is sent anywhere.

sections.title: Update checks go to GitHub
sections.body: Owler checks for a new version once at launch. The check fetches one small file from GitHub Releases, so GitHub sees a request with your IP address, like any download. It carries nothing about your jobs.

sections.title: No analytics
sections.body: There are no crash reports, no usage tracking, no device IDs and no third-party SDKs in the app.

sections.title: You can check all of this
sections.body: Owler is open source under the MIT license. Everything on this page can be checked in the source code. If something looks wrong, open an issue.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: If a future version handles data differently, this page is updated before that version ships.
